learning_outcomes.text: Define a thermodynamic system for practical problems.
Establish mass, energy, and entropy balances for closed and open systems.
Make reasonable, realistic assumptions for subsequent analysis.
Determine material properties (pressure, temperature, density, internal thermal energy, enthalpy, entropy, exergy) using various methods.

Select and apply appropriate thermal and caloric equations of state, steam tables, and state diagrams (especially p,T-, p,v-, T,s-, h,s-, log(p),h-, h_{1+X},X-diagrams) to determine material properties.
Perform calculations and representations of stationary and unsteady reversible and irreversible processes of gases and liquids/vapors.

Understand, calculate, discuss, and evaluate the most important technical cycle processes in terms of their quality (at least Carnot, Joule, Stirling, Philips, Otto, Diesel, Clausius-Rankine, Plank processes).
Present and interpret considerations and results using the usual (graphical) forms of representation (plant schematics, state diagrams, Sankey diagrams) of thermodynamics.
Understand the concepts of relative humidity and water loading and use them to evaluate the consequences of state changes such as heating, cooling, dehumidifying, or mixing.
Recognize heat transfer phenomena and calculate them for simple cases.
Students work in small groups during tutorials, learning about group dynamics in solving technical problems.
Students are able to select suitable methods to systematically analyze thermal machines and systems and evaluate the results.

syllabus_topics: Thermodynamic state variables and changes of state
First and Second Law of Thermodynamics
Energy, mass, and entropy balances of technical systems
Ideal and real gases as well as thermal material models
Cycle processes and thermodynamic processes in technical applications
Heat transfer and energy conversion in thermal systems
Analysis and evaluation of thermodynamic processes and efficiencies
Application of thermodynamic methods to energy technology problems

assessment_methods.method: Passed homework assignments (75% of maximum possible points as prerequisite)

assessment_rules: A graded written exam of 120 minutes duration and passed homework assignments are required. At least 75% of the maximum achievable points from the homework must be obtained to be admitted to the exam.
